idiom_name: typed history entries on the transport headers plus AsyncLocalStorage for in-process hops
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a contract to the JavaScript hash: declare type HistoryEntry = { name: string; at: string } and one readHistory(headers) helper that parses and validates the 'history' key, so every component appends through a single typed function and the header shape cannot drift silently. For hops inside one process (middleware, interceptors, background jobs) AsyncLocalStorage from node:async_hooks carries the same list without touching the message; for hops across services it must still be serialized into the KafkaJS/amqplib header.
pitfalls: Header values in the wild are string | string[] | Buffer: casting to string without narrowing is how a history becomes '[object Object]' or an array of unrelated values.
AsyncLocalStorage context is lost across process boundaries and in some worker/queue conversions, so it complements the header trail and cannot replace it.
A typed key stops typos, not version drift: version the entry shape and tolerate unknown fields when reading partner histories.
